method: Exact integer census of n<=4 adaptive trees; self-contained point-defect finite-to-infinite proof and strict threshold boundary
mathematical_delta: For every n>=3 and every complete adaptive physical restriction tree T of the one-point defect f_n(x)=1-2*1_{x=0} on the uniform n-cube, define bad nodes by B_i(f_v)>2*Inf_i(f_v) and Q_bad(T)=sum_{v bad} pi_v*I(g_v*h_v)/2. Then Q_bad(T)/I(f_n)=(n-1)/2-1/n. Consequently no finite Kprime bounds Q_bad(T)<=Kprime*I(f) for all Boolean f and all complete trees at badness threshold K=2. For every fixed K>2, this same family's Q_bad,K(T)/I(f_n) tends to zero. Its Shannon H/I is less than 4 for n>=2. The universal localized bridge at a sufficiently large fixed K, optimized stopping trees, C018 and FEI are not refuted.
